content.introduction: Immediately upon the release of a lackluster jobs report, bond yields decreased: the 10-year yield went from +5.226% to +5.167%, the 2-year from +4.775% to +4.716%, and the 30-year from +5.592% to +5.572%. Major stock market indexes responded positively: the Dow rose +460 points, the Nasdaq +375, and the S&P 500 +71 points. Semtech (SMTC) saw a +5.66% increase, Viavi Solutions (VIAV) +5.56%, Bloom Energy (BE) +4.75%, NGL Energy (NGL) +3.97%, and The Chef's (CHEF) +3.72%. Labor Force Participation ticked up 20 bps to 61.8%, and the U-6 level was 10 bps lower than anticipated at +7.6%, the lowest since January 2025.
body:
Immediately upon this lackluster jobs report hitting the tape, bond yields started to bid downward: the all-important 10-year went from +5.226% to +5.167%, the 2-year from +4.775% to +4.716%, and the 30-year (which helps predict mortgage rates) from +5.592% modestly lower to +5.572%. Major stock market indexes took these numbers and ran: the Dow rose +460 points, the Nasdaq +375 and the S&P 500 +71 points. [...] | Company | Symbol | Price | %Chg |

| NGL Energy... | NGL Quick QuoteNGL | 16.22 | +3.97% |
| The Chef's... | CHEF Quick QuoteCHEF | 116.75 | +3.72% | [...] Elsewhere, little if any surprises: Average Workweek was steady month over month at 34.4 hours — still historically low. Labor Force Participation ticked up 20 bps from expectations to 61.8%, but this remains on the thin side. The U-6 level — aka “real unemployment” — was 10 bps lower than anticipated at +7.6%, the lowest figure since January of 2025.
